entry.title: Scenario testing for REST APIs: writing user-journey tests from OpenAPI
entry.summary: Single-request testing answers a narrow question: does this endpoint, given these inputs, return this status right now? It cannot answer the question that actually breaks releases: can a user complete the job? A user never calls one endpoint. They create a resource, wait for it to become ready, attach something to it, act on it, and verify the result. Each request depends on the previous one's response. That chain is a scenario, and it is the level where integration bugs actually live. A typical collection has forty green requests. Then production shows: The create endpoint returns an id nested under data.id, but the next request was written assuming id at the root. A list endpoint paginates with a cursor the test never saw because fixtures returned three items. A status field transitions …

entry.title: How I built an AI WhatsApp Auto-Responder with 0% Ban Risk using Google Gemini
entry.summary:
Most WhatsApp bots rely on Python web scrapers that get your phone number banned, or closed-source Play Store apps charging $10/month. I wanted an auto-responder that is completely free, private, and ban-proof. Instead of scraping WhatsApp Web, the app uses Android's native NotificationListenerService and RemoteInput—the exact system API used by Wear OS smartwatches and Android Auto. To WhatsApp's servers, the replies look 100% native. Google Gemini AI: Context-aware, human-like responses instead of rigid regex. Customizable Tones: Professional, Friendly, Chill, Witty, or custom system prompt. Zero Middleman Servers: Direct connection from device to Google Gemini API using your personal API key. Local Storage: All logs stay in your local Room SQLite database. The project is 100% open-source under the MIT license: GitHub Repo: https://github.com/Prince-nebhwani/WhatsApp-Auto-Responder
Live Site & APK: https://prince-nebhwani.github.io/WhatsApp-Auto-Responder/
Feedback and PRs are welcome!

entry.title: What a phone number tells you before you send an SMS
entry.summary: If you send an SMS to a landline it disappears. No bounce, no error you can act on, and you are still billed for it. The same goes for a disconnected number and for plenty of VoIP numbers. The fix is to find out what a number actually is before you send to it. Here is what a phone number can tell you, and what it cannot. Start by normalizing to E.164 07400 123456 -> +447400123456 First, a national number with no country code is ambiguous. 07400123456 is a UK mobile, but a bare 7400123456 could belong to several countries. You need a default country to parse against, usually the country of the account that submitted the number. Second, people paste extensions, letters and stray leading zeros. entry.title: Solana RPC 服务商定价指南:别只看每月多少钱,到底该怎么比?
entry.summary: 比较 Quicknode、Helius 和 Triton One 三家 Solana RPC 服务商的定价机制,拆解"按链""按方法""按次数+流量"三种计费逻辑,教你如何根据自己的实际调用情况算出真实成本,而不是只看每月套餐价格。
